title: The recoil nucleon effect in nuclear systems
summary: Nuclear excitation energies are typically in the keV-MeV range, but rare eV-scale transitions remain a puzzle for nuclear theory. This work develops a two-body recoil model to describe $β^-$ decay on the basis of classic momentum conservation. Using the final states of $β^-$ decay with a keV-scale excitation energy, the model yields eV-scale recoil energy for a single nucleon. It indicates the recoil nucleon effect in nuclear systems: a single nucleon bound in a nucleus can be excited by absorbing the recoil momentum. The observed eV-scale isomers in $^{235}$U and $^{229}$Th can be attributed to the recoil neucleon effect. This effect could spark a eV-scale energy, and provide a solid theoretical foundation for predicting such extremely small energies. The new discovery will place low-energy nuclear isomer research at the cutting edge of new-physics searches, while offers a clean and complementary alternative to high-energy accelerator experiments.

title: Exploring the phase diagram of dense and hot matter with HBT interferometry
summary: We investigate the HBT radii of pions produced in Au+Au collisions at selected energies from the STAR-BES program, using an event-by-event hybrid model that combines AMPT initial conditions, 3+1D viscous hydrodynamic evolution with a QCD equation of state at finite baryon chemical potential, and hadronic transport with SMASH. The goal is to explore the source's space-time structure and its possible connection to the structure of the QCD phase diagram. The hybrid chain was first validated by comparing identified-particle spectra and anisotropic flow, yielding a globally consistent description of the experimental data, with more evident discrepancies at the lowest energies.

title: Antinucleon--nucleon interaction at next-to-next-to-leading order in covariant chiral effective field theory
summary: We construct antinucleon--nucleon ($\bar NN$) interactions at next-to-leading order (NLO) and next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in covariant chiral effective field theory. The short-range interaction is represented by complex covariant contact terms, while the long-range part is obtained from the corresponding nucleon--nucleon interaction through $G$-parity transformation. The low-energy constants are determined from the Nijmegen partial-wave analysis, and phase shifts and mixing angles are calculated for all partial waves with $J\leq2$. Compared with NLO, NNLO improves the overall description of the phase shifts and mixing angles, particularly in several $J=2$ channels, although the improvement is not uniform across all partial waves or at higher energies. We estimate Bayesian truncation uncertainties and compare the results with heavy-baryon chiral interactions. We also revisit the pole candidates identified in our leading-order study and calculate the corresponding threshold parameters. The isoscalar ${}^{13}P_0$ pole remains a few MeV below the $\bar NN$ threshold with a width of about 40 MeV at both NLO and NNLO, whereas the $S$-wave candidates show stronger sensitivity to chiral orders. The NNLO covariant $\bar NN$ interaction therefore provides a useful basis for studies of antinucleon--nucleon scattering and near-threshold phenomena.

title: New $γ$-softness in $^{196}$Pt from $γ$-rigid triaxiality
summary: The interplay between the $γ$-softness and the $γ$-rigidity is a key aspect in understanding nuclear collectivity. In this paper, the $γ$-softness emerging from the $γ$-rigid triaxiality within the framework of the SU3-IBM is applied to investigate the $^{196}$Pt nucleus. The SU(3) fourth-order interaction, $\hat{C}_{2}^{2}[\text{SU(3)}]$, which introduces the rigid triaxial degree of freedom, is treated as an essential component of the Hamiltonian. Based on this, we systematically calculate the low-lying energy spectra, B(E2) transition rates, and quadrupole moments for $^{196}$Pt. The agreement between experimental data and theoretical calculations demonstrates that the present approach provides an effective explanation for the observed features.

title: Measuring the Neutrino Mass with $^{241}$Pu
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to SciPost Physics. Code: https://github.com/AnaamMustafa/Pu241-Neutrino-Mass-Supplement
summary: Tritium has long been the isotope of choice for measurements of the absolute neutrino mass. Its low nuclear mass leads to substantial recoil energy, limiting measurements with both molecular tritium ($T_2$) and atomic tritium bound to a substrate. With a beta-decay endpoint energy and half-life similar to those of tritium, but a much larger nuclear mass, $^{241}$Pu may offer an interesting alternative. Its principal challenge is background from the beta decay of $^{237}$U. We discuss strategies for suppressing this background and compare the projected neutrino-mass sensitivities of $^{241}$Pu and tritium as a function of the background suppression.

title: Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) optimization of residual correction of $α$-decay energy based on Weizsacker-Skyrme 4 model
summary: A physics-guided hybrid framework combining the Weizsacker-Skyrme-4 (WS4) macroscopic-microscopic mass model with the Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) is developed to improve the accuracy of alpha-decay energy predictions for superheavy nuclei. TabPFN learns the residuals between experimental data and WS4 predictions using nuclear-structure features. Through ablation studies of 18 feature combinations, the optimal feature set is identified, reducing the overall root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 0.2743 to 0.1442 MeV, an improvement of 47.43%. The corrected model improves prediction accuracy across all four odd-even nuclear configurations while preserving shell effects and odd-even staggering patterns along the Po, Rn, and U isotopic chains. The framework is further applied to predict decay energy values for experimentally unmeasured nuclei along the Z = 118-120 isotopic chains. The extrapolated results retain the overall trends of WS4 and exhibit signatures associated with the predicted neutron shell closure at N = 184. These findings highlight the potential of physics-guided residual learning for predicting the decay properties of superheavy nuclei.

title: Bypassing the Nanoampere Limit: A Thick-Target Methodology for Ultra-Low-Energy Resonances in the $^{11}$B(p,$α$)2$α$ Reaction
summary: Precise measurements of the low-energy cross section for the $^{11}$B(p,$α$)2$α$ reaction is critical for nuclear astrophysics and fusion energy research, yet such measurements are experimentally demanding due to the reaction's extremely small cross section. Conventional thin-target experiments are fundamentally limited to nanoampere beam currents, which restrict count rates to impractical levels at ultra-low proton energies. To overcome this limitation, we report a correction-free thick-target methodology capable of operating at beam currents of 20-60 microamperes, corresponding to a gain of over three orders of magnitude. Monte Carlo simulations of the full reaction kinematics are employed to determine the absolute reaction yield, eliminating the requirement for empirical normalization factors. At the well-known 148~keV (c.m.) resonance peak, our extracted resonance energy ($E_{\mathrm{r}} = 148.0$~keV) and level width ($Γ_{\mathrm{cm}} = 5.3$~keV) are demonstrated in good agreement with published data. A scheme via comparing the measured reaction probability with a theoretical extrapolation result is furtherly presented to probe low-energy resonances below 100~keV region. Preliminary measurements at proton energies of 75~keV and 100~keV reveal no evidence for additional low-energy resonances. This work provides a robust new methodology to measure cross section and resonance parameters for the p$^{11}$B reaction and offers a highly efficient tool for systematic resonance searches in the ultra-low-energy regime.

title: Weak magnetism effects on neutrino-nucleon interactions in hot nuclear matter within nonrelativistic Skyrme RPA
summary: Neutrino production, absorption, and scattering are important in explaining neutrino-driven core-collapse supernovae. At high densities or temperatures, relativistic effects, in particular weak magnetism (WM), may become increasingly important. Therefore, we extend the nonrelativistic random-phase approximation (RPA) framework for the study of neutrino-nucleon interactions in hot nuclear matter by incorporating the WM term into the nucleon weak current. In calculations with our recent Skyrme functional Sky3s, we confirm that WM increases interaction rates for the most important charged-current neutrino processes in supernovae and reduces those of antineutrinos. However, this is not the case for the antineutrino production via $β$ decay, which is also increased. In our calculations, WM can almost double the neutrino emissivities of neutron-star matter by direct Urca processes at high density. We also find that WM corrections to the scattering rates are increasingly important with increasing scattering angle and energy transfer, leading to a significant difference between double-differential neutrino and antineutrino scattering rates. Our formulas can help improve neutrino rates needed in supernova simulations.

title: Probing radial flow via the differential flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ using CMS open data
summary: We present a comprehensive study of the differential radial flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ and its $p_T$-integrated counterpart $v_0$ in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$, using CMS open data for mid-peripheral centrality classes of 50--60\% and 60--70\%. The measured $v_0(p_T)$ distributions are compared with ATLAS measurements at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, revealing a clear energy dependence in the overall magnitude of radial flow fluctuations. Notably, the scaled ratio $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ exhibits an approximate universality that is largely independent of both collision energy and centrality at low $p_T$, persisting up to $p_T\sim3~\mathrm{GeV}$, suggesting that the integrated $v_0$ encodes most of the energy-dependent information. We compare the data with the \textsc{Jetscape} multi-stage hybrid model, using Gaussian process emulators trained on a principal component analysis of the model output to explore the full 17-dimensional parameter space. A global variance-based sensitivity analysis using Sobol indices shows that, for the Grad viscous correction, the nucleon fluctuation parameter $σ_k$ is the dominant source of variance for $v_0$, $v_0(p_T)$, and $v_0(p_T)/v_0$, followed by the free-streaming parameters $τ_R$ and $α$ and the nucleon width $w$. The sensitivity to the bulk viscosity peak $(ζ/s)_{\max}$ is weak for $v_0$ but increases for $v_0(p_T)$ and for the scaled ratio. Emulator predictions, calibrated on $p_T$-integrated observables and on scaled spectra, describe the data reasonably well at low and intermediate $p_T$. Parameters calibrated at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$ also describe the ATLAS $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ data at $5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, supporting a near universal momentum dependence of radial flow fluctuations across collision energies.

title: Sampling nucleon short-range correlations in coordinate and momentum space for Au+Au collision simulations
summary: We develop a nuclear initialization scheme that jointly incorporates spatial nucleon correlations, high-momentum components, predominantly proton-neutron pair assignments, and correlated pair momenta, and implement it in the SMASH transport model. This construction enables controlled comparisons of the effects of different ingredients of short-range correlations (SRCs) on heavy-ion observables. For Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.4$ GeV, SRC initialization increases both charged-pion yields relative to a Woods-Saxon reference with Fermi momenta when the same mean-field parameters are used. The larger relative enhancement of $π^+$ production reduces the $π^-/π^+$ ratio. Controlled comparisons identify the modified single-nucleon momentum distribution as the dominant source of the enhancement, with smaller effects from the tested spatial and pair-isospin variations and enhanced production persisting without the imposed pair-momentum structure. Reaction histories link this enhancement to increased baryon-resonance production. Stronger high-momentum repulsion counteracts the SRC-induced pion enhancement by reducing the energy available in nucleon-nucleon collisions and suppressing resonance production. The similar enhancement of $K^+$ production with SRC initialization and its reduction after refitting the mean-field parameters show that the competing effects of correlated initialization and mean-field dynamics extend beyond pion production.

title: Emergence of collectivity in the $0^+_2$ band of $^{92}$Zr
summary: The $2^+_2 \rightarrow 0^+_2$ transition in $^{92}$Zr was observed for the first time in a high-statistics decay study of the 10-day isomer $^{92m}$Nb. Its $E2$ transition strength of 8.9(7) W.u. is enhanced by 40% relative to the ground state band, providing evidence for a collective structure built on the $0^+_2$ state which is analogous to the deformed shape-coexisting configuration in $^{94}$Zr.

title: Coulomb-Induced $K^- pp$ Molecular State
summary: We studied a new bound state in the three-body system consisting of an antikaon and two nucleons. The state is primarily induced by the Coulomb interactions between the $K^-$ and the two protons, and is modified by the strong $K^- p$ and $pp$ interactions. This spatially extended molecular state has binding energy and width that are of the order of keV, compared to the tens of MeV binding energy and width of the famous quasi-bound $K^- pp$ state caused primarily by the strong interaction.

title: Revealing Nuclear Shape through Identified-Hadron Flow Decorrelations
summary: Relativistic nuclear collisions encode nuclear shape in collective flow, yet the potential of identified hadrons to disentangle deformation modes remains largely unexplored. Using event-by-event viscous hydrodynamics coupled to hadronic transport, we investigate momentum-dependent elliptic-flow decorrelations of pions, kaons, and protons in central $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U collisions at 193 GeV and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions at 5.36 TeV. The identified species exhibit distinct momentum- and deformation-dependent responses, with nuclear-shape information persisting in their relative correlations even when individual deformation effects are weak. We introduce crossing coordinates $(P_{\rm cross},R_{\rm cross})$, defined by the intersection of pion-kaon and pion-proton flow-factorization ratios. Variations of quadrupole deformation and triaxiality generate distinct trajectories in the crossing plane, offering complementary constraints on both nuclear-shape parameters. The corresponding behavior persists in higher-moment correlations, while an energy comparison in Ne+Ne reveals the influence of collision dynamics. Our findings establish identified-particle flow decorrelations as a complementary approach to probing and constraining intrinsic nuclear geometry.

title: Neutron-alpha scattering on a quantum processor: Spin-orbit-split resonances and weak nonresonant channels
summary: We reconstruct elastic neutron--alpha phase shifts in all five channels through $l=2$ from trapped spectra measured on IBM's Boston quantum computer. Using a four-qubit implementation of the factorized geometric-time RODEO algorithm, we resolve the spin--orbit-split $p_{3/2}$ and $p_{1/2}$ resonances of $^5$He and the small nonresonant $d$-wave phase shifts. Classically constructed eight-dimensional effective Hamiltonians are encoded in three system qubits and probed with a recycled ancilla. We fit 40 trapped energies per channel at five confinement strengths (200 energies in total), using a reciprocal effective-range function for the $d$ waves. The fits yield free-space phase shifts, the elastic cross section, and both $p$-wave poles. The broad $p_{1/2}$ pole is more sensitive to the fit order. On the $0.05\leq E_{\rm cm}\leq6$ MeV grid, the reconstructed phase shifts differ by less than $0.073^\circ$ from an independent radial calculation for the same calibrated interaction. The maximum relative difference in the $l\leq2$ cross section is $0.185\%$. In separate measurements of ten low-lying levels in three time-separated blocks, reversing the evolution times and query phase changes the fitted energies but leaves the ideal ancilla-history probabilities unchanged. Averaging forward and reverse estimates reduces the pooled root-mean-square energy error from $49.59$ eV for forward evolution alone to $20.91$ and $16.37$ eV in two retrospective equal-shot comparisons. The effect varies by channel. Histogram tests reject the working noise model for most hardware scans, so the conditional fit errors do not quantify the total hardware uncertainty.

title: Emulator-enabled calibration and uncertainty quantification of $β$-decay calculations within the energy density functional theory
summary: Predictions of $β$-decay half-lives of neutron-rich nuclei and their uncertainties critically impact our understanding of the astrophysical rapid neutron capture process. To provide quantified predictions within nuclear energy density functional theory, as customarily done, we perform Bayesian calibrations of two coupling constants: the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing strength and the isovector spin-density coupling. We apply an E-optimal experimental design for choosing the calibration sets. We employ the proton-neutron finite-amplitude method with Skyrme energy density functionals using emulators of half-lives and Gamow--Teller resonance energies. The calculated $Q_β$ values are fine-tuned to experimental values. The contributions to the half-life uncertainty from the theory error, $Q_β$ values, and the parameter uncertainty are all accounted for in the Bayesian framework. Our predictions for the even-even $N=126$ isotones provide the shortest half-lives for neutron-rich nuclei among the existing theoretical models, which would affect the flow of heavy-element nucleosynthesis. The proposed framework allows quantified theoretical uncertainties to be propagated to astrophysical observables such as abundance patterns and electromagnetic emission.

title: Hint of universality in $α$-cluster nuclei
summary: The empirical ground-state energies of the $α$-cluster nuclei are placed on the universal function that governs $N$-boson systems with a shallow state. The data fall on the finite-range-corrected universal curve, suggesting Efimov-type universality. No excited states, transition strengths, radii, or cluster geometries enter the analysis; the nuclei are treated as $N$ structureless bosons. A zero-shape $α$-$α$ Bargmann potential, describing the $^{8}$Be resonance, provides the pairwise interaction with no shape freedom. Simple three- and four-body forces, each a single Gaussian in the hyperradius, are fitted to $^{12}$C and $^{16}$O; microscopic calculations for $^{20}$Ne and $^{24}$Mg ($N=5,6$) follow as parameter-free predictions. A compact $0^+_2$ state near the Hoyle energy emerges in $^{12}$C without being targeted by the fit.

title: 1+1 dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration
summary: We study $(1+1)$-dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration under the conformal equation of state $\varepsilon=3p$. We evolve temperature, fluid rapidity, and shear stress using energy conservation, longitudinal momentum conservation, and a shear-relaxation law in a prescribed transverse magnetic stress. Moving beyond longitudinal boost invariance, we derive perturbative analytical expressions in the Navier--Stokes approximation and obtain nonlinear solutions with shear relaxation, comparing dynamical and prescribed accelerating flows from identical initial conditions. The initial temperature curvature generates a longitudinal pressure gradient that alters the rapidity slope, modifies longitudinal expansion work, and produces a distinct cooling history. For the reference parameters, shear viscosity enhances the resulting central temperature difference much more strongly than the prescribed magnetic stress, while the condition for equal central temperatures shifts with proper time and initial shear. At $χ=λ^*=0.03$, the maximum relative difference in central temperature is $0.18\%$ over $0.6$--$6$~fm/$c$, despite a persistent momentum residual in the prescribed flow. Because the velocity mapping also enters the entropy per unit fluid rapidity, the rapidity distribution remains sensitive to the flow evolution even when central temperatures closely agree. Replacing the prescribed field with ideal induction removes direct magnetic work while retaining magnetic pressure and inertia in the longitudinal momentum balance.

title: Toward the Centennial of Wigner's Supermultiplet Symmetry: an Ab Initio Perspective
summary: As the centennial of Wigner's supermultiplet theory approaches in 2037, this review offers a modern perspective through the recently advanced ab initio Symmetry Adapted Model (SAM). We begin with the symmetry's empirical foundations in two-nucleon data and electroweak processes, and trace its emergence from the strong force through effective field theories, the QCD large-$N_c$ limit, the similarity renormalization group, and lattice calculations. We then follow its historical arc, from early limited engagement, through its revived interest, to the modern algebraic and first-principles resurgence. Central to this renaissance are new nullspace-based algorithms for the U(3) and U(4) coupling and recoupling coefficients, which remove a bottleneck spanning nearly nine decades and are released as the open-source libraries u3lib and u4lib. Building on them, the SAM is the first large-scale ab initio shell model to encode both Elliott's spatial U(3) and Wigner's spin-isospin U(4) symmetries, resolving individual supermultiplets that share the same quadratic Casimir eigenvalue. Early results show that the spin-isospin symmetry strongly dominates high-fidelity chiral interactions and suppresses spin-isospin polarizability in light nuclei. We close with potential directions that the SAM is poised to advance within the next decade.

title: Finite Temperature Isoscalar Instabilities and Moat Regimes in Relativistic Nuclear Matter
summary: We study the finite-temperature isoscalar collective response of symmetric nuclear matter in three relativistic mean-field descriptions: the linear Walecka model, its nonlinear extension, and the quark-meson coupling (QMC) model. The Walecka models are formulated in terms of nucle- onic degrees of freedom, whereas QMC incorporates quark degrees of freedom confined inside the nucleon. These models differ in their treatment of scalar interactions at finite density, affecting instability boundaries. Focusing on the coupled scalar-vector channel, we track how the boundaries of homogeneous instabilities evolve with temperature. In all three models, we find a nonmonotonic momentum dependence of the static response, characterized by a minimum at finite momentum, a moat regime that selects a preferred length scale for density fluctuations. Our results show that this moat structure is robust against thermal effects across these relativistic nuclear matter models, providing motivation for future studies of inhomogeneous phases in hot and dense astrophysical matter.
